$comment: One SDK for the whole tree. The 10.0 SDK builds every target here: net8.0 (the pure core and
the client), the add-in shim (net8.0-windows or net10.0-windows) and the suite's net8.0/net10.0 pair.
The shim compiles against Revit 2025's API, NOT the newest installed, and its target framework
follows that API's runtime: a net8.0 project referencing an API built for .NET 10 fails with
CS1705 ('uses System.Runtime 10.0.0.0 which has a higher version'), and the 2025.5 update moved
Revit 2025 to .NET 10. revit/README.md, Build and test, holds the table.
rollForward latestFeature keeps this on 10.0.x: a machine with a newer 10.0 patch band builds
without editing this file, and a machine with only 8/9 fails loudly instead of silently
